info.bio:
A los 15 años, Joan formó The Runaways con otras tres rapadas, Sandy West, Lita Ford y Cherie Currie. Joan cantaba, tocaba la guitarra rítmica y escribía mucho material de la banda. La banda grabó cinco LPs y giró por todo el mundo entero junto con Cheap Trick, Van Halen, Tom Petty y The Heartbreakers. Tuvieron especialmente éxito en Japón.

Mientras que The Runaways eran muy populares en Europa, Japón, Australia, Canadá y en Sudamérica, ellas no tuvieron el mismo éxito en Estados Unidos.

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El heavy metal renace en los mismos años que la new wave, aprovechando los sellos independientes: Motörhead (puente entre metal, Stooges/MC5 y punk), Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Diamond Head, Def Leppard y, en EE UU, Van Halen. Entre 1982 y 1985 el subgénero gótico se convierte en «black metal» (Venom, Mercyful Fate, Celtic Frost, Helloween, Bathory). El pop-metal y el shock-rock (Twisted Sister, Mötley Crüe, Joan Jett, Bon Jovi, Savatage); la pompa y el doom (Manowar, Voivod, Saint Vitus, Pentagram); el metal progresivo (Living Colour, Queensrÿche, King's X, Pantera, Joe Satriani) y el «street sound» de Los Ángeles (Guns N' Roses, Jane's Addiction, Faster Pussycat).

podcast.title: Kim Fowley's Training Method
podcast.body: Kim Fowley, the manager of The Runaways, prepared the band for live performances by having road crew members throw various items like bottles and paper at them during rehearsals. This method was intended to familiarize the band with the challenging reactions they might face on stage. "Kim Fowley, who was the manager of the runaways, actually prepared the band for playing live by having the road crew throw junk at them, bottles, paper, whatever, while they were rehearsing, just so they knew what they were getting into."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rock Credibility and Chart Performance
podcast.body: Joan Jett is cited as an example of female vocalists of earlier generations who "had to rock pretty hard" to achieve rock credibility. She successfully made Billboard's rock tracks charts, distinguishing her from Madonna and Pink in terms of genre categorization on the charts. "Janice Joplin, Tina Turner, Joan Jet, and Pat Benatar have all made Gilboard's rock tracks charts."

podcast.title: Signature Gibson Melody Maker
podcast.body: Joan Jett's primary guitar for many years was a white Gibson Melody Maker, which she acquired from Eric Carmen after The Raspberries disbanded. This guitar was famously used on The Raspberries' hit "Go All The Way" and is heard on many of Jett's own successful songs. She later collaborated with Gibson on her own signature Melody Maker models, released in 2008 and 2010. "For the longest time, Joan Jett's main guitar has been a white Gibson melody maker."

podcast.title: Trailblazer and Rhythm Player
podcast.body: Joan Jett is recognized as a trailblazer in rock music, primarily for her hard-riffing rhythm guitar style rather than virtuoso soloing. Her pioneering spirit, especially as a member of The Runaways, places her as a significant figure. "Joan belongs on this list because she was a trailblazer."

xref.title: Formation and Inspiration (1975)
xref.body: The Runaways were formed by producer Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the success of the all-female band Fanny. Active from 1975 to 1979, they are arguably recognized as the first all-female hard rock band, featuring future stars Joan Jett and Lita Ford. "The first is to a weirdo producer named Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the group to form the Runaways, arguably the first all-female hard rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Attempted Bowie Bonds
xref.body: James Brown was one of several artists who attempted to replicate David Bowie's financial innovation, the Bowie Bonds, by securitizing his own music royalties. "Other artists tried the same thing. James Brown, the songwriting team of Holland Dozier Holland, the Isle of Brothers, Ashford and Simpson, even the guy who wrote songs like I Love Rock and Roll for Joan Jett, and another songwriter who wrote songs for Rod Stewart and Tupac."

xref.title: First All-Female Hard Rock Band with International Attention
xref.body: The Runaways, anchored by 15-year-old Sandy West on drums, are identified as the first all-female hard rock band in history to gain international attention. The group featured future stars like Joan Jett, Lita Ford, and Mickey Steele, along with Cherie Currie and Jackie Fox. "We can safely call them the first all-female hard rock band in history to receive international attention."

xref.title: Juno Awards 50th Anniversary Performance
xref.body: The surviving members of The Tragically Hip reunited to perform at the 50th anniversary of the Juno Awards on June 6th, 2021, with Feist filling in on vocals. There was initial "resistance amongst all of us to delve back in and open that door," but the decision was made due to the significance of the 50th anniversary, the honor being received, and the desire to support musicians and live venues during a period of hardship. Feist was suggested as a singer, and the band felt "everyone had that same response," believing Gordon Downie would approve. The performance was compared to Nirvana's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction performance with female vocalists like Lorde, St. Vincent, Kim Gordon, and Joan Jett. "if there was a time when we were going to entertain the idea that this is probably it."

xref.title: Kim Gordon's Diverse Inspirations
xref.body: Kim Gordon drew inspiration from a wide range of female artists across different genres, including punk icons like Patty Smith and the Slits, Goths like Suzy Su, rockers like Joan Jett and The Runaways, blues singers like Billie Holiday, and her ultimate heroine, Tina Turner. "She was inspired by the women who came before her. There were punks like Patty Smith and the slits, Goths like Suzy Su, Rockers like Joan Jaden, The Runaways, Blues singers like Billie Holiday, and her greatest heroine, Tina Turner."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Popularizer of the "Bo Diddley Beat"
xref.body: Bo Diddley is renowned for using a particular rhythm so effectively that it became known as the "Bo Diddley beat." Although the beat itself originated at least 50 years before his time, he was instrumental in introducing it to rock and roll, influencing numerous artists from Iggy Pop to Joan Jett. "Bow didn't invent that beat. It's history goes back at least 50 years, but he was the one who introduced it to rock and roll."
